about.title: Personal Injury Help in Albany, California
about.longDescription: Albany is a small city, but its streets carry a steady stream of regional traffic. Corridors like I-80, Marin Avenue, Solano Avenue, and San Pablo Avenue see heavy use from commuters, shoppers, and cyclists alike, and that volume shows up in the numbers. In the most recent year on record, Albany logged 66 injury collisions, with 89 people hurt and 1 traffic death. Collisions tend to cluster on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m., when work traffic, school pickups, and weekend errands overlap. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, you're not alone, and you don't have to figure out next steps by yourself. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Albany with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we never charge you a fee. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no cost unless they recover money on your behalf. Reaching out costs nothing and puts you in touch with someone who can explain your options clearly.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Shared Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of blame is fairly assessed.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages — like pain and suffering — in a typical injury case. That means your recovery isn't artificially limited by a legal ceiling.

items.title: You Risk Nothing to Ask
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost and no fee unless money is recovered for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Albany?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle or public roadway, the deadline to file a notice can be as short as six months. It's wise to speak with an attorney early so you don't lose your right to pursue compensation.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover damages even if you share some blame. Your total compensation is simply reduced by the percentage of fault assigned to you. An attorney can help ensure that percentage is calculated fairly.

items.question: Where do injury collisions tend to cluster in Albany?
items.answer: Public collision records show that corridors like I-80, Marin Avenue, Solano Avenue, and San Pablo Avenue account for a notable share of reported injury crashes in the city. Reported incidents also tend to peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral, public-record patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and there's no cost to connect with an independent attorney through us. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In a typical California personal injury case, there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. The amount depends on the specifics of your situation, including the severity of your injuries and how they've affected your life.
